# Code style and patterns

## Tooling

The workspace declares `bun@1.2.20` and has `bun.lock`; use Bun and the app's package scripts. This app has no configured lint/format script. Do not borrow sibling ESLint settings or invent a formatter command.

TypeScript uses `strict`, `isolatedModules`, `noEmit`, ES2020 target and `react-jsx`; `@/*` maps to `src/*`. Use explicit types for boundaries and `unknown` with narrowing for new untrusted values. Existing `any` usage is not a reason to widen new APIs.

## Formatting and imports

- Match surrounding two-space indentation and semicolon-free TypeScript; quote style varies in existing files.
- Preserve the workspace `CLAUDE.md` import rule: `// ** import types`, `utils`, `lib`, `apis`, `constants`, `styles`, with one blank line between sections and abstract-to-concrete ordering.
- Existing entry points additionally group core packages and assets. Do not churn unrelated imports.
- Use `import type` for type-only imports, `@/` for app aliases, relative imports for colocated modules, and extensionless TS imports as surrounding code does.
- Components/types use PascalCase (`Status`, `SavedForm`); helpers/hooks use camelCase (`getSettings`, `useSpeech`); constants use upper snake case (`DEFAULT_SETTINGS`).

## State, errors and UI

- Keep DOM behavior in the content/picker/filling modules and Chrome storage/network boundaries in their existing adapters.
- Reuse native controls, shared primitives and semantic tokens. Use layout styles for composition, not a second control skin. See [DESIGN.md](../../DESIGN.md) and [UI-SYSTEM.md](../UI-SYSTEM.md).
- User-facing failures use the shared `Status` component and safe error-message extraction. Messaging commonly returns `{ success, error }`; callers must check success before claiming completion.
- Preserve drafts and save behavior when changing layout. Cleanup listeners/timers and ignore stale async results where needed.
- Avoid reading or displaying API keys in diagnostics, screenshots or test logs.

## Tests

Bun tests live under `tests/<domain>/*.test.ts` and import from `bun:test`. DOM tests use `tests/helpers/dom.ts` and Happy DOM. Prefer tests of meaningful behavior and safety, not CSS implementation details. The local `tests/e2e/serve.ts` harness and `ui-review.cjs` inspect production output with stubbed Chrome APIs; they cannot establish live provider or installed-extension permission behavior.
